pharm: A carbamate derivative of guaifenesin that relieves muscle spasm through central nervous system depression rather than direct action on skeletal muscle, used as an adjunct for acute painful musculoskeletal conditions and historically in tetanus.
quick: Oral: 1500 mg QID x48-72h (6 g/day), then ~1000 mg QID (~4 g/day)
May be taken with or without food; with food if GI upset
Category C; avoid unless benefit outweighs risk (fetal abnormalities reported)
Excretion in human milk unknown (present in dog milk); use caution
Injectable contains polyethylene glycol - caution/avoid IV in renal impairment
Half-life prolonged in cirrhosis; use with caution
Sedation, blood pressure (IV), injection site, mental status
summary: Methocarbamol is a centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant used as an adjunct to rest, physical therapy, and analgesics for the relief of discomfort from acute, painful musculoskeletal conditions, and parenterally in the management of tetanus. Its action is attributed to general CNS depression; it does not directly relax skeletal muscle or block neuromuscular transmission. The usual oral adult dose is 1500 mg four times daily for the first 48-72 hours (up to 8 g/day in severe cases) reduced to about 4 g/day for maintenance. The main adverse effects are drowsiness and dizziness. The intravenous preparation contains polyethylene glycol 300, so it should be used cautiously in patients with renal impairment.
indications: Adjunct to rest, physical therapy, and other measures for the relief of discomfort associated with acute, painful musculoskeletal conditions
Adjunctive control of the neuromuscular manifestations of tetanus (parenteral)

dosage.d: 1500 mg (three 500 mg tablets) four times daily
dosage.n: 6 g/day for first 48-72 hours; up to 8 g/day for severe conditions

dosage.d: About 1000 mg four times daily, or 1500 mg three times daily, or 750 mg every 4 hours
dosage.n: Reduce to ~4 g/day after the first 48-72 hours

dosage.d: 1000 mg (10 mL) up to 3000 mg/day for no more than 3 consecutive days
dosage.n: Max IV rate 3 mL/min; do not exceed 5 mL into each gluteal IM site; transfer to oral as soon as feasible

dosage.d: 1000-2000 mg into IV tubing initially, then up to a total of 3000 mg; may repeat every 6 hours
dosage.n: May give via gastric tube as crushed tablets once feasible; adjunct to definitive tetanus management

dosage.d: 15 mg/kg or 500 mg/m2 IV, repeated every 6 hours as needed
dosage.n: Maximum 1.8 g/m2/day for 3 consecutive days if needed

admin: Oral tablets may be taken with or without food; take with food if stomach upset occurs
For IV, do not exceed 3 mL per minute; the patient should be recumbent during and for 10-15 minutes after injection to limit hypotension/dizziness
For IM, give no more than 5 mL (500 mg/mL = 2500 mg) into each gluteal region
Avoid extravasation and subcutaneous injection - the hypertonic solution can cause thrombophlebitis/sloughing
Limit parenteral use to 3 consecutive days and switch to oral therapy as soon as possible
moa: Methocarbamol is a centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant whose mechanism of action in humans has not been clearly established. It does not directly relax tense skeletal muscle, depress neuronal conduction, neuromuscular transmission, or muscle excitability. The muscle-relaxant effect is generally attributed to its central nervous system depressant properties, which may interrupt polysynaptic reflex arcs involved in the production and maintenance of muscle spasm.

absolute: Known or suspected hypersensitivity to methocarbamol or any component
Injectable form: known or suspected renal pathology, because of the polyethylene glycol 300 vehicle (risk of further renal injury and acidosis)
relative: Pre-existing CNS depression or use of other CNS depressants
Myasthenia gravis on anticholinesterase therapy (may inhibit the effect of pyridostigmine)
Seizure disorder (seizures reported with IV use)
monitor: Level of sedation and ability to perform tasks requiring alertness
Blood pressure, heart rate, and signs of fainting during/after IV administration
Injection site for thrombophlebitis or extravasation
Renal function when using the injectable formulation

preg: Pregnancy Category C. Safe use in pregnancy and lactation has not been established; there have been reports of fetal and congenital abnormalities following in-utero exposure. Methocarbamol should not be used in women who are or may become pregnant, particularly during early pregnancy, unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the possible hazard.
lact: Methocarbamol and/or its metabolites are excreted in the milk of dogs; it is not known whether they are excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects in the nursing infant, caution should be exercised; consider the benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential risk.
renal: The injectable preparation contains polyethylene glycol 300, which may be harmful in patients with renal impairment (risk of further renal injury and accumulation/acidosis); the injectable form is contraindicated/avoided in known or suspected renal disease. Methocarbamol clearance is reduced about 40% in patients undergoing hemodialysis. Use the oral form cautiously in renal impairment.
hepatic: The elimination half-life is prolonged in patients with hepatic cirrhosis (about 3.4 hours versus 1-2 hours in healthy adults) and clearance is reduced; use with caution and consider lower doses in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Other CNS depressants (alcohol, benzodiazepines, opioids, sedatives, antihistamines) - additive sedation and respiratory/CNS depression
Pyridostigmine bromide / anticholinesterases - methocarbamol may inhibit their effect (use caution in myasthenia gravis)
minor: May cause color interference with certain urine laboratory tests (5-HIAA, VMA)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol - it produces additive central nervous system depression.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause falsely elevated/colorimetric interference in urinary 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) and vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) assays.

rare: Thrombophlebitis and extravasation injury at injection site
Metallic taste, fever, conjunctivitis with nasal congestion
emergency: Severe hypotension or syncope after IV dosing
Coma/respiratory depression (overdose, especially with alcohol/CNS depressants)

monitoring: Degree of sedation and ability to operate vehicles/machinery
Blood pressure, heart rate, and mental status during and after IV use
counsel: This medicine may make you drowsy or dizzy - do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you
Do not drink alcohol or take other sedating medicines with it
Use it together with rest and physical therapy for short-term relief; it does not cure the underlying problem
Your urine may turn brown, black, blue, or green - this is harmless
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down to avoid feeling faint
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, have kidney problems, or have myasthenia gravis
pk: Plasma Tmax about 1-2 hours after oral dosing
About 1-2 hours (up to ~3.4 hours in cirrhosis)
Store tablets at 20-25 C; injection at 20-25 C, do not refrigerate
pearls: Centrally acting - works via CNS depression, not direct muscle relaxation
Front-load to 6 g/day (up to 8 g) for 48-72 hours, then taper to ~4 g/day
Injectable contains polyethylene glycol 300 - avoid IV in renal impairment
Patient must be recumbent during IV use and limit IV rate to <=3 mL/min to avoid hypotension/seizures
Causes harmless dark/discolored urine - reassure patients
Can interfere with urinary 5-HIAA and VMA assays (carcinoid/pheochromocytoma workups)
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose.
overdose: Overdose produces nausea, drowsiness, blurred vision, hypotension, seizures, and coma; deaths have occurred, usually in combination with alcohol or other CNS depressants. There is no specific antidote. Treatment is supportive - maintain airway, breathing, and circulation; gastric decontamination/activated charcoal if appropriate; IV fluids and pressors for hypotension; and seizure control. The usefulness of hemodialysis is not established, though clearance is partly dialyzable. Contact a poison control center.
